title: One package describes, checks and fingerprints every data shape
Every outbound connection follows one policy, and data leaves only with a permit
A proxy set only in the operating system's settings is used
Every package in the binary that can open a connection is accounted for
A component is told when a file or directory changed, on every filesystem
Globs and versions each have one meaning
Instants and recurrence rules each have one meaning
Small leaf packages give errors, identifiers, the home location, media types and bounded output one form
Pick lists filter one way, and a tool card reads arguments while they arrive
Any area can test real components against scripted boundaries, in virtual time, and leave nothing behind
A recorded session replays against the built binary without a key and proves the transcript and the files
A run states which evidence it holds: scenarios count only when they passed, boundaries only when fuzzed
schema lives at src/harness/internal/schema and is the only importer of its module
The util family is a leaf, and a helper needs two consumers to enter it
Each upstream utility gets one of four placements, and merged ones name their owner
The language replaces helper packages: distinct types, bounded queues, context deadlines, plain values
egress is a service that adds one header, asks for a permit, and builds child environments by audience
Fakes exist only at seams, pass the seam's own suite, and fail on anything unscripted
A fixture is a session export; replay is a stream listener bound by lineage that checks the request
A scenario is declared through one helper, every outcome is a report row, and only a pass counts
Closed root by default, every out-of-subset path listed, all violations returned, one importer of the schema module
Form decoding, changed-path reporting for live fields, provider projection with listed losses, duration fields as text
Every egress client sends the one identity header, keeps no cookie, and is listed until its owner unloads
A sharing client needs a permit, and ending the permit cancels the request in flight
Child environments by audience, resolution only through the given lookup, and the idle body in virtual time
A watch is released with its owner's fiber, and the manual fake passes the real service's behavioural table
Cron fixed-hour and wildcard-hour rules across clock changes, and latest-at-or-before for every rule kind
Coded errors are found through wrapping, reasons have one form, the home resolver follows its precedence, and the language table agrees with the highlighter
Retained text never splits a rune and the omitted count is exact
The streamed-argument reader gives the same answer for every fragment split and decodes only requested values
Import rules for util and testkit hold, and each own analyzer rejects a seeded violation
A full bounded queue behaves as declared, and a tool body that ignores cancellation fails the conformance helper
The composition harness loads a shipped bundle through the real loader and fails a test that leaks an effect or goroutine
The scripted model fails on unscripted and unconsumed calls and passes the adapter conformance table
The fault server's behaviours and per-key cursors, and the egress recorder's refusal of unlisted requests and lookups
A committed fixture is a fixed point of normalisation and an unscrubbed fixture fails its guard
Concurrent child sessions each receive their own recorded script by lineage
Replay fails on a request that differs, replays a recorded failure without a sidecar, and the runner ends the whole process tree
A skipped scenario is a recorded row, a required one that cannot run fails, and the checker fails a required scenario with no pass
A marked trust boundary without a fuzz target fails the analyzer, and a committed crasher runs under plain go test
All traffic goes through a real TLS-intercepting proxy
A required scenario that cannot run fails the acceptance job
Zone rules resolve on a machine with no zone database
A proxy set only in the system settings is used, and a PAC address is named
The small helpers stay narrow on purpose
The operating system's static proxy setting is read once at launch, below every environment variable; a PAC address is reported, never evaluated
The system proxy reader parses recorded Windows and macOS settings, reports a PAC address without fetching it, never stops a launch, and ranks below every environment variable
Every package in the binary's import graph that can open a connection is in a reviewed table with a supply path

reason: Atomic file replacement and the writer lock are provided by the fsx package that area A08 owns: Replace stages, optionally syncs and renames, and the lock is a kernel file lock instead of a lock file holding a process ID.

Branded string and number types exist because TypeScript types are structural; each confusable identifier becomes a defined Go type declared by its owner, which the compiler keeps distinct, so no helper package is needed.
The persistent chunked list gives frozen projection state cheap appends; in Go a fold owns an append-only slice and hands readers a capped view, which is an immutable snapshot at no copying cost.
The extension-to-language table becomes the Language function of the mediatype leaf package, beside the media-type table, and gains whole-file-name rules; the host-side highlighter reads it.

The UUID helper exists because browsers lack randomUUID on plain-HTTP pages; the Go host mints every identifier through the ident leaf package on crypto/rand, and base64 comes from the standard library.

The circular deque avoids linear-time array shifts in JavaScript; a Go queue is a bounded channel or a bounded slice ring inside its one owner, and its declaration states what happens when it is full.

The dependency-free error base with a stable machine-readable code is kept as the herr leaf package: an error value carrying a domain/reason constant declared by the package that owns the failure, found with errors.As.
Safe export file names from a declared media type become SafeName in the mediatype package; the native drag requests served the desktop application, which the owner removed.

The one resolver for the harness home (explicit path, DSH_HOME, then ~/.dsh, blank counted as unset), tilde expansion and symbolic display are the homedir leaf package; the layout under the root is area A07's and watch-path canonicalisation moves inside the watch service.

The one outbound proxy policy is kept and becomes the egress service: every HTTP client, WebSocket dial and telemetry export is built by it from values resolved once at launch, instead of replacing a process-wide dispatcher.

The frozen, layered launch environment with a recorded source per value is the launch.Env value that area A21 builds before the tree; egress and other readers receive a lookup over it and nothing reads the process environment directly.
Caller-relative lazy loading of CommonJS modules exists only because of Node's module system; a Go binary is linked statically and a deferred initialisation is sync.OnceValue.

The shell-free run-and-capture wrapper is the capture helper of the one process package that area A09 owns; of the path-opening functions only the default-browser hand-off is kept, and revealing a file or listing its applications is not built because the web UI has no native shell integration.

The compiled-in lists of npm bundle packages become the embedded bundles, profile layers and optional list of the boot family (areas A27 and A21): every component is already in the binary, so a list entry is a default-off loader entry.
The bounded-retention primitive is kept as the retain leaf package, with head, tail and head-and-tail windows for both text and items, rune-safe cuts and an exact omitted count.

The shared TypeScript declarations of package.json plugin fields become the one plugin manifest struct that area A22 owns; a Go struct with schema validation is declaration and validator at once, and a plugin is a local directory, not an npm package.

The fixed, localised fallback order for a plugin's long description is kept over the local plugin directory and belongs to area A22; the npm file CDN and repository sources go because nothing is downloaded.

The market index validator has no reader: the owner decided that plugins come from local directories and that nothing is discovered or downloaded; a later registry would define its own format behind the same manifest.
Resolving and spawning a packaged rg executable is replaced by file search in process, in pure Go, in the search package area A08 owns; there is no executable to locate.
The tiered multilingual filter for in-memory lists is kept as the textsearch leaf package with an own scorer; lists are filtered on the host.

The shared time vocabulary is kept as two leaf packages: caltime (strict instant and zone parsers, the gap and overlap resolver) and recur (cron, RRULE, interval and wall-time rules behind one Rule interface with Next and Resolve).

Deadline arithmetic, signal fusion and timeout-versus-cancel classification are context.WithTimeoutCause and context.Cause in the standard library; the idle watchdog becomes egress.IdleBody; termination stays with each capability as upstream decided.

Lossless-JSON checks, snapshots, deep freezing, structural equality and exhaustive-switch helpers compensate for untyped, shared JavaScript objects; Go uses typed values, copies and the schema package. The lazy reader of streamed tool arguments is kept as the jsonscan leaf package.

Browser-safe lexical path helpers exist because client code cannot touch a file system; the host resolves paths and renders titles (area A07) and file addresses become HTTP routes (area A19), so no shared package remains.

Mounting the loop's prerequisites and driving a production agent is the compose package of the test kit, which boots real components through the real loader with a scripted model; the two Inbox stubs are not carried because fakes exist only at seams.

The jsdom slot bench and whole-client tier test a React client that the Go design does not have; server-rendered fragments are tested with golden files and HTML query helpers through the real handlers.
The scriptable fault server is kept as testkit/faultserver with upstream's behaviour list, per-key script cursors, and a deterministic scripted refusal at the egress seam.

Keyless replay of recorded model streams is kept as the llm.replay component: a listener on area A04's stream interception point plus a stub route registration, with scripts bound to child sessions by lineage and the live request compared with the recorded one.

Booting a fixture's real entry point in a child process is done by testkit/dshbin, which builds the dsh binary once per run and runs it with a private home, capped output and whole-tree termination; the source-versus-built mode switch has no Go counterpart.
The package mocks Typert Remote traffic between upstream's JavaScript browser client and its host; the Go design has no Typert layer and no client program, so there is nothing to mock.

Recorded-session testing is kept in the Go design's own formats: the test/replay runner with one driver per surface, typed normalisation tokens, a typed scenario manifest, workspace comparison and fixture guards.

Fixture tools and tool execution without a full turn are kept in the test kit: a fixture tool is declared like any tool and called through the pipeline's direct-caller entry on a real in-memory session, and a conformance helper checks that a body honours cancellation.

Replaced by the Go struct replay.Config with Scenario (one directory instead of three file paths), Mode and Pace; the provider catalog comes from the recorded request headers and no environment variable supplies a default.

Final verdict: change the mechanism, keep the split. Go's context package already gives deadlines, fused cancellation and a recorded cause, so no timeout library is written; the rule that each capability keeps its own hard kill and that there is no central timeout service is kept, and the idle watchdog becomes egress.IdleBody.

Final verdict: keep. One resolver, the homedir leaf package, decides the home in the order explicit path, DSH_HOME, ~/.dsh, with a blank variable counted as unset and all user data under one root; three documents had named three different owners for it and this specification settles it.

Final verdict: keep the policy, change the mechanism. The policy is still resolved once from the launch environment and a project file may not choose the proxy, but nothing is installed globally: the egress service builds every client, which also covers the WebSocket and telemetry traffic upstream's dispatcher missed.

Final verdict: change. One documented manifest is kept, but it is a Go struct for a local plugin directory, owned by area A22 and validated by the schema package, so the note's rule that every reader parses and validates for itself no longer applies.

Final verdict: change. The goal (an experimental capability is visible and one switch away) is kept; with every component compiled in, an optional bundle is a default-off loader entry on area A27's optional list, and the admission test of npm install cost has no subject.

Final verdict: keep. A lazy reader over streamed argument text avoids re-parsing a growing JSON text on every delta; it is the jsonscan leaf package, used by the host that renders the preparing row, and the rule that short descriptive fields are declared first carries because schema properties follow struct declaration order.

Final verdict: keep. One vocabulary for instants, zones and recurrence, with parsers that return a stable reason and callers that own their error text, is the caltime and recur packages; the Duration class is replaced by time.Duration and zone names are no longer rewritten.

Final verdict: change. Heavy integrations stay discoverable without being paid for by everyone, but nothing is installed on demand: the integration code is compiled in and its catalog entry reports whether the operator-installed external runtime is present.

Final verdict: keep, simplified. The error base stays in a package with no dependencies (herr) so that any package can return a coded failure without importing the model runtime; the re-export that kept one class identity is unnecessary because errors.As matches by type.

Final verdict: drop, which corrects the first verdict of replaced. The owner decided that the harness downloads and discovers no plugin, so no index document is read; a registry added later behind the same manifest would define its own identity and version fields.

Final verdict: change. A deterministic, localised fallback order for a plugin's detail page is kept, stated over the local plugin directory and its manifest by area A22; reads from npm file CDNs and repositories are gone with plugin download.

Final verdict: change, which corrects the first verdict of ported. The purpose (an operator can tell what may be deleted and what must be backed up) is met by the home layout area A07 already specifies, which is new and needs no migration; the five category directories are not adopted, and A07 is asked to state the category of each top-level directory.

Final verdict: change. Shipped but switched off becomes a compiled-in component that no shipped layer mounts and that a layer edit can enable; the npm runtime-dependency rules and their isolation gate have no subject.

Adapters, optional components, load order and teardown are no longer the caller's: compose.Start loads a named bundle and extra layers through the real loader, registers a scripted model, and unloads the tree in the test's cleanup.
The composition harness registers the scripted model on a default route unless the test supplies its own, so a test that starts the loop has an adapter without wiring one.
The process-local Inbox stub is not carried: a consumer test builds a real agent on an in-memory store, so durable events, projections and claim policy are always the production ones.
The fail-fast Inbox stub is not carried either; a test that must prove the inbox is untouched asserts that the real session log holds no inbox event.
The limit concerns generated zod Remote clients of upstream's JavaScript browser client; the Go design renders HTML on the host and has no generated client to bypass.
The limit concerns the JavaScript Gateway client's invoke path being bypassed by a test proxy; there is no Gateway client in the Go design, and UI tests call the real HTTP handlers.
The limit concerns how a JavaScript Remote proxy guesses unary or stream mode for an undeclared endpoint; the Go design has no Remote proxy.
The limit is a TypeScript compile-program detail (Node ambient types leaking into client sources); Go has one type-checked program and no ambient type sets.
The limit concerns separate fixture types for the React client's Session, Conversation and Chat stores; the Go UI has no client stores, and a page is rendered from host state.
The fault server's random mix is still test pressure and not an estimate of how often a provider fails; it prints its seed so that a run can be repeated.
justification: A fault distribution is an input chosen by the test author by nature; measuring a real provider's failure rates is outside what a test fixture can do. DH-D-UTIL-6 keeps the seeded mix and its statement.

reason: The Go fault server keeps one script cursor per key computed from the request by a test-supplied function, so concurrent callers no longer share one arrival-ordered cursor and one server instance gives deterministic per-caller faults.

A refused connection no longer depends on overlapping a listener's start-up delay: the egress test recorder scripts a dial failure for a chosen attempt, which is deterministic and needs no real listener.

A live child session is bound to its recorded script by its lineage (the parent's script and the ordinal of the tool call that created it), not by which session calls the model first, so siblings that run concurrently bind deterministically.

Narrowed, not removed: every attempt, failed ones and summariser calls included, is one logged event in the Go design, so a failure before the first chunk is derived from the log; a hang is still not a recorded fact and needs an authored override file.
justification: Non-termination cannot be recorded as an event, because a recording is finite. DH-ADR-UTIL-7 limits the override file to hangs and authored scripts and DH-D-UTIL-7 builds it.

reason: Built mode needing a prior build exists because upstream runs either TypeScript source under tsx or bundled output under Node; go test compiles what it runs and the kit builds the dsh binary itself, once per run, from the build cache.
The binary runner caps captured output at a budget the test states and fails the test naming the cap, instead of inheriting a 100 MB default from a process library.

The binary runner starts the child through the one process package, whose operating-system job object or process group ends the whole tree at the deadline, so a tree spawned by a faulty fixture cannot outlive the test.
An in-process-only carrier is a limit of a mock for the JavaScript client's Connection object; the Go design has no such client and tests the HTTP surface with net/http/httptest.
Values crossing by reference instead of being serialised is a property of an in-realm JavaScript mock; Go UI tests go through real HTTP handlers, where everything is serialised.
Unchecked answer envelopes are a limit of the Typert Remote mock; there is no Typert result envelope in the Go design.
Endpoint-only rule matching is a limit of the Typert Remote mock, which has no Go counterpart; a Go fake is scripted per call and fails on anything unscripted.
Native stream overrides bypassing the mock's log concern Vitest mock functions over JavaScript async iterables; nothing of the kind exists in the Go design.

The replay runner harvests a session through the product's export command, which writes the line-per-event export format whatever the store's internal encoding is, so no storage mode has to be configured for tests.
Built mode needing current artifacts exists because of upstream's source-versus-bundled split under Node; the Go kit builds the binary it runs from the same packages the tests compile.

A behaviour whose stimulus is a protocol client (an ACP cancellation or permission round trip) is still replayed through that protocol's driver; the runner has one driver per surface and a scenario names the one it needs.
justification: This is a rule, not a defect: driving a protocol behaviour through another surface would not test it. DH-D-UTIL-7 builds the drivers behind one interface.

reason: A fixture tool is declared through the same declaration path as a product tool, with a typed output and a derived schema, so there is no special content-array fixture form that differs from production.

The kit has no way around the pipeline: a direct tool call enters the guarded pipeline's direct-caller entry on a real in-memory session, so it is logged, and batch scheduling is exercised by a scripted-model turn.
Composition and disposal belong to the composition harness, which unloads the tree in the test's cleanup and fails the test when an effect is left.
File replacement can be durable: the caller states it and the file and its directory are synced before success is reported (fsx.Replace with Durable, owned by area A08).
The Go replacement takes a function that writes to the staged file, so content can be streamed and need not be complete in memory.
The writer lock is a kernel file lock, released by the operating system when its holder dies; there is no lock record to be empty and no process ID to be reused, so no orphan needs an operator.
Nothing probes a process ID any more, so a different PID namespace cannot make a live holder look dead; a harness home must be on a local filesystem and one that is not is refused instead of raced.
Append-only access is a limit of a persistent list built because JavaScript state is frozen and shared by reference; a Go fold owns an ordinary slice, which has random access.
Recursive checkpoints come from the linked-chunk structure and the JavaScript runtime's nesting limits; a Go slice is stored as one flat JSON array.
The Language function matches whole file names as well as extensions, so Dockerfile, Makefile and dot files without a suffix are recognised.
A file with no known name or extension is still shown as plain text; the table never reads content.
justification: Guessing a language from bytes the model or a user wrote would change rendering unpredictably; the only content verdict the design makes is text or binary, in area A08's fsx. DH-D-UTIL-5 keeps the name-only rule.

reason: The double registration is gone: the host has one highlighter and a test asserts that every language id in the table is one the highlighter accepts, so adding a language is one reviewed change. The table stays curated.
Callers treat an identifier as opaque and obtain it from one function, so its form can change in one place (for example to a time-ordered form) without a second helper or dependency.
Identifiers are still random and unique only with overwhelming probability; the helper detects no collision.
justification: This is inherent in random identifiers with 122 random bits. Where uniqueness matters the store enforces it with a key constraint, so a collision would be a refused insert and not silent sharing. DH-ADR-NODECRYPTO-2 keeps one helper.

reason: A queue without a capacity policy cannot be declared: every in-process queue is a bounded channel or bounded buffer whose declaration states what happens when it is full.
An export file name is still derived from the declared media type and an explicit suffix still wins; content is not inspected.
justification: Media types are answered from the name by one compiled-in table so that the answer is the same on every machine (requirement R3 of the mime library specification); sniffing content would break that. DH-D-UTIL-5 keeps the rule in SafeName.

reason: Only a bare ~ and ~/ expand; named-user forms, environment variables and shell expressions in a path are left unchanged.
justification: Expanding variables or shell syntax in a path would let a config value evaluate against the environment outside the one explicit mechanism for that, the restricted expression language of DH-ADR-LOADER-3. DH-D-UTIL-5 keeps the narrow rule.

reason: Consumers no longer canonicalise a watch path themselves: the watch service accepts a path that may not exist, resolves it by file identity and follows it when parents appear or vanish; directory creation and permissions belong to the home layout.
SOCKS5 proxy URLs are now accepted, which removes a third of the limit. Proxy auto-configuration files and the operating system's proxy settings are still not read.
justification: Reading system proxy settings needs WinHTTP calls on Windows and a cgo framework on macOS, and the core binary must be pure Go (DH-ADR-15). DH-D-UTIL-2 reports an unusable value by variable name so the operator knows to export the variables.

reason: Go verifies against the operating system's trust store, and an operator setting adds certificate authority files to it; an unreadable file stops the launch with its path.

The host itself no longer depends on a Node version, but a Node child it starts (an MCP server, for example) still routes through the proxy only if that program's runtime reads the variables it is given.
justification: The harness cannot change how a third-party program makes connections. DH-D-UTIL-2 gives a trusted child the user's own values and the resolved ones for names the user left unset, which is all a parent process can do.

reason: Telemetry is no longer direct: the exporter takes its HTTP client from egress, so proxy and certificate policy apply, and the client is created only for a permit holder.

The guest runtime and workflow worker do not exist; a model-written program is an ordinary command, and its environment is built for the ModelRun audience: proxy values without credentials are passed, a value carrying a password is omitted and the omission is reported once.
The static check for clients built outside egress still sees only this repository's source, not the inside of a dependency.
justification: A source analyzer cannot follow calls into third-party modules. The design narrows the gap: the egress test recorder fails any composition test in which a request or name lookup bypasses it, and a module that cannot accept an http.Client is not adopted (DH-ADR-UNDICI-1).

reason: The launch environment is never written into the process environment, and the one spawn helper builds each child's environment explicitly, so a discovered project variable reaches a child only if a rule passes it on.
The launch environment is still read once from the invoking directory; a workspace chosen later contributes nothing.
justification: Kept on purpose, as upstream states: following a workspace would let a directory the model can write change the harness environment in the middle of a session. Area A21 carries the same limit for its own unit.

reason: The CommonJS-only limit is a property of Node's two module systems; Go has one linker and no module loading at run time.
The limit concerns the WebWorker packer's static discovery of JavaScript dependencies for the in-browser preview runtime, which is dropped and has no Go counterpart.
The run-and-capture helper of the one process package takes an explicit output budget and offers streaming, instead of rejecting on a fixed buffer limit inherited from Node's execFile.

The limit describes icon extraction for the application picker of upstream's Electron and Node desktop integration; the Go design has no desktop application and builds no list of applications that can open a file.

The one hand-off that remains, opening the web UI in the default browser, still needs an interactive desktop session on Windows; in a service or SSH session the launcher can report success having opened nothing.
justification: This is operating-system behaviour the harness cannot change. The launch always prints the URL as well, and the hand-off has a deadline, so a failed open costs nothing but the convenience (the browser hand-off of DH-LIB-OPEN).

reason: There is no list a profile cannot extend: every compiled-in component can be named by a loader entry, so a layer can enable or add any of them without a release. Only the set of components itself changes with a release.
The item retainer supports head, tail and head-and-tail windows, each with an exact omitted count; pagination and grouping stay with the tool because they are not truncation.
Go strings are UTF-8, so there is one unit: a budget in bytes is cut on a rune boundary by the same retainer, and the separate UTF-16 surrogate helper has no counterpart.
The plugin manifest is a Go struct decoded strictly through the schema package by one reader, so parsing, validation and defaults exist once instead of in every consumer.
A declared harness version range is enforced: it is parsed strictly when the manifest is inspected and a plugin that requires another host version is refused before it starts.
The public-npm-only limit concerns reading a package's files from npm file CDNs; in the Go design a plugin is a local directory and nothing is read from npm.
The limit concerns a generator's obligations toward an index of npm packages; the Go design reads no market index because plugins are not discovered or downloaded.
The missing size bound concerns parsing a fetched npm market index document, which the Go design never fetches or parses.
Search runs inside the host in pure Go, so no executable has to be co-located and a remote provider needs no rg binary.
With in-process search there is no record stream to split and decode: a path is a Go string holding the file system's bytes unchanged, so a name with a newline or invalid UTF-8 stays usable.
The filter still matches substrings and letters in order from a word start; a transposed or wrong letter does not match.
justification: A pick-list filter that also guesses at typing errors returns matches the user cannot explain; the tiers are fixed by golden tests so that order is predictable. DH-D-UTIL-5 keeps the rule, and the UI areas may ask for more.

reason: Lists are filtered on the host, which holds the message catalogue in every language, so a label that comes from the catalogue can be matched in all languages and not only the active one.
File reference ranking remains a separate ranker in area A08's search package; the plugin market index is not built at all.
justification: Ranking paths in a large tree is a different problem from filtering a short pick-list, and one package for both would serve neither well. DH-D-UTIL-5 covers pick-lists only.

reason: Zone names are validated and stored exactly as given and never rewritten to a canonical alias, so no answer depends on the zone data of a particular runtime build.
Recurrence stays a bounded subset: five-field cron and the RRULE subset and limits upstream accepts, with a rejection that says whether the cause is syntax, zone or density.
justification: Kept on purpose by DH-ADR-RRULE-1: the subset is what the model was taught, and the limits are what guarantee bounded work when resolving after long downtime. DH-D-UTIL-4 builds it.

reason: The limit documents an own Duration class written because TypeScript arithmetic erases a branded number; Go's time.Duration is a distinct elapsed-time type and calendar steps are done on a time in its zone.
The limit concerns how much of the own TypeScript Duration class is published; the Go standard library's time.Duration is complete and there is no class to grow.
A span in configuration is a time.Duration field that the schema package reads from text such as 30s, and arithmetic uses that type, so no call site multiplies a bare number of seconds by a thousand.

Loading the recurrence dependencies with the package root is a cost of JavaScript module entry points and browser bundles; Go links only imported packages, caltime and recur are separate, and no time code runs in a browser.
A deadline is still a notification: cancelling a context cannot stop work that ignores it, and every capability keeps its own way to end a process, socket or task.
justification: Go cannot stop a goroutine from outside. The design bounds the effect: process-owning code ends the process tree, and a conformance helper in DH-D-UTIL-6 fails any tool body that does not return when its context ends.

reason: There is no zero-or-negative sentinel: no deadline is expressed by not setting one, and a configured timeout is a duration field whose schema bounds reject zero.
The first cancellation cause still wins: when an upstream cancel arrives before the local timer, the record says cancelled and cannot also say the timeout would have fired.
justification: One recorded cause per cancellation is what makes the record on turn/end unambiguous (DH-ADR-ARCH-3), and context.Cause has the same rule. DH-ADR-UTIL-4 adopts it.

reason: The idle timer on a response body still measures silence on the wire only; it is not a limit on total time and does not count the consumer's own pauses.
justification: The two questions are different by definition; a total limit is the deadline on the request's context, and a caller that wants both sets both. DH-D-UTIL-2 names them separately (IdleBody and the context).

reason: A JSON-only structural comparator exists because JavaScript has no value equality for objects; Go compares typed values directly, so there is no general comparator whose input assumptions need stating.
deepFreeze and its gaps exist because JavaScript objects are shared by reference; the Go design keeps data immutable by ownership and copying and freezes nothing.

WeakMapWithValues works around JavaScript weak references; a Go registry is owned by a fiber and each entry is an effect released on unload, which is the explicit cleanup the limit asks callers to remember.
Lexical-only resolution is a limit of code that must run in a browser, which cannot access a file system; in the Go design the host resolves paths through the filesystem seam.
Home abbreviation is POSIX-only because a browser cannot know the host's Windows home directory; the Go host knows it on every system and abbreviates before rendering.
The marker asks for an explicit ordinal for concurrent child sessions; replay binds a child by its recorded lineage (parent script and creating tool call ordinal), which is that explicit key.

The marker asks for a replacement that syncs the file and its directory and keeps owner-only permissions on Windows; fsx.Replace does both (the Durable and KeepPerm options), in the package area A08 owns.
